subject: Meaning of the output from stat_smooth?

messages.author: 972c5c093ee9ac8f
messages.subject: Meaning of the output from stat_smooth?
parts:
Hi,

Firstly thanks to those involved with creation and maintenance of
ggplot2 - it has really revolutionised how I analyse much of my data,
and the ease at which I can ask new questions means I can ask more
than previously.

I have a probably naive question regarding stat_smooth. Basically, I'm
wondering what exactly the line and standard error represent. The help
at http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/stat_smooth.html suggests that the method
is this:
method: smoothing method (function) to use, eg. lm, glm, gam, loess,
rlm

However the default is "auto". I don't quite understand what "auto"
means, though - can someone enlighten me? I was unable to find an
answer on the help pages or a quick google, but I'm known to be blind
sometimes.

Thanks in advance,
ben

I'm not sure where (or if) it is documented, but auto is equivalent to
"loess" when there are fewer than 1000 rows in the data and is
equivalent to method="gam", formula=y~s(x, bs="cs") if there are 1000 or
more rows (this function is from the "mgcv" package).
